analysis.title: The momentum massacre: two 6-sigma shocks in one week
key_insights: October was the worst month for the momentum factor in more than 40 years, per JPM, including two 6-sigma unwind days in roughly one week. Cap-weighted momentum underperformed the market by 10.8%, a -5.8 sigma event.

Long/short momentum lost 16% during October. Combined with the July unwind, the cumulative momentum drawdown is 30%, the largest since ChatGPT launched, which erased a year of momentum outperformance.

JPM estimates Equity Long/Short funds lost about 3% in October, Multi-Strats about 3% and Equity Quant funds 4-5%. Asia-focused Quant funds lost 7-8%. The Multi-Strat damage ranks among the worst in history, comparable to the dot-com collapse, Lehman and COVID episodes.
JPM argues forced liquidation of crowded AI exposures may have been more severe than in July.

JPM says the October hedge-fund liquidation produced a more favourable positioning backdrop for equities, particularly AI stocks. Momentum crowding fell from the 100th to the 86th percentile of its 40-year history and sits at the 12th percentile versus the past three years. Longer-term crowding remains elevated.

JPM does not expect hedge funds to return to AI quickly. It sees a few weeks of stability, supported by retail buying, as the potential catalyst for renewed institutional exposure from late November onwards.
Retail flows are weakening. Weekly retail flows are $2.5bn versus a 12-month average of $6.5bn, with single-stock outflows of $2.3bn.

sector_views.rationale: JPM says the hedge-fund liquidation reset positioning, making the backdrop more favourable for AI stocks, with the next surprise potentially to the upside.

risk_factors: Retail buying is fading: weekly flows of $2.5bn versus a $6.5bn 12-month average, with $2.3bn of single-stock outflows.
Longer-term momentum crowding remains elevated despite the reset.
Hedge funds may not return to AI exposure until late November or later, so the market needs a few weeks of stability first.
vol_and_positioning: Momentum factor had two 6-sigma unwind days in roughly one week in October, which JPM calls a disorderly positioning unwind rather than a normal rotation.
Momentum crowding fell from the 100th to the 86th percentile over 40 years and is at the 12th percentile versus the past three years.
Hedge fund losses in October: Equity L/S about 3%, Multi-Strats about 3%, Equity Quant 4-5%, Asia Quant 7-8%.
JPM sees a possible year-end squeeze as positioning has reset, but it depends on retail holding up until hedge funds return.
